_provenance.what: The ancestors' eclipse readings of eclipses.json, as structured rows the saṃskāra can take (scripts/parampara-samskara.cjs). Every value is taken from that file's own 'gloss' fields; nothing is added from any other source.
_provenance.site: Parameśvara's village on the Nilā: palabhā 2 aṅgula 18 vyaṅgula and deśāntara −2°, as ss-grahana.test.js builds it from JM p.36.
_provenance.padas: A shadow 'of n padas' is a man's shadow in his own foot-lengths. The script turns it into the shadow of the text's 12-aṅgula śaṅku as n × 12 ÷ man_padas, with man_padas = 7 [unverified convention: no local text states it], and reports the result for 6.5 and 7.5 as well.
_provenance.side: Only SDip-77 says which half of the day ('in the afternoon'). For the others the record does not say; they are read as forenoon (pūrva) [reading], and the script also prints each such row's residual if it were afternoon.
_provenance.excluded: SDip-82 (day unresolved in the source), JM-Syanandurapura and JM-Harihara (their towns' positions would need modern geography, and the text puts both eclipses a day earlier: council KH-05), and the Gokarṇa halves of SDip-69 and SDip-70 (Gokarṇa's position likewise).
_provenance.day: Each row's day is the record's printed ahargaṇa; the text's eclipse is searched from noon of that day.
